title: Fix DirectML GPU acceleration silently falling back to CPU
description: Provider logging (daz-content-browser-67l) revealed DmlExecutionProvider was unreachable: chromadb and optimum both pull in plain onnxruntime transitively, which shares its import namespace with onnxruntime-directml, and whichever gets installed last silently wins. install.py's docs also still claimed CPU-only, left over from before the DIM-packaging commit (de19ddc) switched pyproject.toml's intent to DirectML-with-CPU-fallback. Force-reinstall onnxruntime-directml last in install.py/Makefile so it reliably wins, and update docs/messages to reflect GPU-with-fallback. Benchmarked ~7.3x faster embedding inference on DirectML vs CPU once warmed up (0.59ms/item vs 4.32ms/item).
design: Root cause: onnxruntime and onnxruntime-directml are separate PyPI packages sharing the 'onnxruntime' import path; pip has no way to express their mutual exclusivity, so transitive deps (chromadb, optimum) silently reinstall plain onnxruntime over the intended DirectML build with no error or warning at install time.
acceptance_criteria: install.py and Makefile both force-reinstall onnxruntime-directml --no-deps as the last dependency step; embedding_utils.py log line confirms DmlExecutionProvider active after a fresh install; existing test_embedding.py and tests/test_api.py pass.
close_reason: Fixed install order in install.py and Makefile; verified DmlExecutionProvider stays active after force-reinstall, test_embedding.py and tests/test_api.py pass, ~7.3x speedup confirmed via benchmark.

title: Skip re-embedding unchanged products on full reindex
description:
Full reindex (--all/--force) re-embeds every product's embedding_text on each run, even when most products are unchanged since the last index. This wastes ONNX inference time and ChromaDB upsert work at scale.

Add a checksum (e.g. sha256) of embedding_text per SKU, stored alongside the product row in SQLite. During generate_and_store_embeddings(), compare the new checksum against the stored one and skip embedding+upsert for SKUs whose text hasn't changed. Only embed new/changed/missing-from-Chroma SKUs.

This is a cheaper, more broadly impactful win than the existing I/O pipelining optimization (daz-content-browser-8wq) since it avoids the embedding work entirely for unchanged items rather than just overlapping it.
close_reason: Incorrect premise: incremental update only ever processes brand-new SKUs (postgres_skus - sqlite_skus), never re-touches existing ones, so there's nothing unchanged to skip there. --force/--all is intentionally a from-scratch rebuild, so checksum-skipping would undermine its purpose. No real benefit.

close_reason: Logging added and verified by running load_embedding_model() directly: confirmed DmlExecutionProvider is not even in the available providers list on this onnxruntime build, active provider is CPUExecutionProvider.

title: Morph ingest: add retry/error visibility for embed_and_store_morphs failures
description: embed_and_store_morphs (src/managers/morph_transpiler.py) returns only an embedded count; unlike its sibling generate_and_store_embeddings (src/managers/postgres_db_manager.py) which returns a success/failure bool, a fully-failed embed batch is invisible to the CLI (src/main.py discards the return value). Combined with incremental mode only ever passing new_guids to the embed step, a batch that fails after SQLite has already committed those rows is never retried on a later run (hashes match, so it's skipped) -- a permanent gap with no equivalent of 'vab load --phase embed' to repair it for morphs.
acceptance_criteria: Caller can detect a partial/failed embed run (e.g. non-zero exit code or explicit log/warning), and there's a documented way to re-embed already-ingested-but-not-embedded morphs (a --phase-embed-only style flag, or a query for SQLite-guids-missing-from-Chroma using the existing ChromaDbManager.get_all_ids()).

title: Morph ingest: harden incremental cache against stale/moved/deleted files
description: Several related incremental-mode gaps found during final review of the morph ingest pipeline (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-06-morph-ingest-transpiler.md): (1) the skip-on-hash-match branch never checks that the referenced .tmb file still exists on disk, so deleting morph_cache/ alone (without also touching morph_index.db) leaves rows pointing at missing files that a future consumer would fail to read; (2) a .dsf moved within the library (same mtime+size, different path) is skipped as unchanged, leaving a stale source_dsf_path/tmb_path; (3) .dsf files deleted from the library are never pruned from morphs/morph_cache -- only --force clears everything. (4) morph_cache/ is not in .gitignore, so a default-path run drops a large untracked tree in the repo root -- fix this one immediately, it's a one-line addition.
acceptance_criteria: morph_cache/ added to .gitignore. At least the missing-.tmb-file case (1) is detected and triggers re-ingest of that row rather than silently trusting a stale hash match.

title: Morph ingest: validate --library-path before destructive --force actions

The destructive actions should happen after path validation, not before.
acceptance_criteria: A --force run with a nonexistent --library-path fails fast with no destructive side effects (Chroma collection intact, morph_cache/ and morph_index.db untouched).
close_reason: Extracted validate_library_root(), called before any destructive --force action in both index_library and the CLI, verified with test + manual CLI check

title: Morph ingest: scope name-marker dependency resolution to target_figure, not global name

A pathless formula ref (name:X) can therefore bind to a same-named morph on the wrong figure. Should be keyed on (target_figure, name) instead. Found during final-review fix-wave re-review; rated Minor only because morph_dependencies has no consumer yet, but becomes real the moment anything reads the graph (e.g. the future C++ injector).

close_reason: Scoped name_to_id lookup to (target_figure, name) in rebuild_dependencies, test added and passing

title: CLI Progress/Rich spinner crashes with UnicodeEncodeError on cp1252 Windows terminals
description: Both 'vab load' and the new 'vab morphs index' use rich.progress.Progress with a SpinnerColumn. On a Windows terminal running the legacy cp1252 codepage (not UTF-8 console mode), Rich's spinner cleanup on Progress.__exit__ raises UnicodeEncodeError ('charmap' codec can't encode character u2826) when writing the braille spinner glyph. Discovered while smoke-testing the new morphs index command against a real DAZ library subset (X:\DAZ Libraries\Project data) — the underlying ingest/embed work completed successfully (verified 70/70 morphs in SQLite + Chroma) but the process then crashed with a traceback instead of printing the final summary line. Pre-existing in load_command's identical Progress setup; not introduced by the morph ingest work, just newly triggered by it.
acceptance_criteria: vab load and vab morphs index both complete cleanly (exit 0, summary printed) on a Windows terminal running the default cp1252 codepage, e.g. by disabling Rich's legacy Windows rendering or forcing UTF-8 output mode.

title: Scope standalone CLI/offline indexer (no DAZ Studio, no FastAPI server)
description: Discussed with user: a standalone tool for users with very large content libraries to pre-build the index outside of DAZ Studio, avoiding resource contention with DAZ's own CPU/GPU usage while indexing runs. Key insight from discussion: the indexing logic is already factored into a reusable function (run_update_flow in api_tasks.py), so this is cheap to build as a thin CLI entry point calling it directly -- no FastAPI server needed. The GPU/threading speed itself benefits equally whether called from the server or a standalone tool (DirectML/threading work helps both paths identically) -- the standalone tool's real value is avoiding contention with DAZ Studio's own resource usage, not raw speed. Would need packaging as an optional DIM (similar to the existing export-tool package pattern in release.py) and the settings dialog should clearly show when an index was built externally so users aren't confused about why 'Update Index' shows nothing new to do. Not yet scoped in detail -- needs a design pass before implementation.

title: Pipeline embed-loop I/O with compute (overlap SQLite reads/Chroma writes with ONNX inference)
description: Discussed as a follow-up to the DirectML fix (daz-content-browser-0ce/i8z): generate_and_store_embeddings (postgres_db_manager.py:217-292) does SQLite read -> ONNX embed -> ChromaDB upsert sequentially per batch with no overlap. Now that DirectML is confirmed genuinely active and fast (~7.3x vs CPU), the SQLite/Chroma I/O around it is proportionally larger and may be worth overlapping with a producer/consumer pattern (prefetch next batch's SQLite read while current batch embeds/writes). Keep ChromaDB upserts serialized since its local SQLite-backed store isn't documented-safe for concurrent writers. Lower priority now than before the DML fix landed, since GPU embedding speed reduced how much this matters in absolute terms — re-evaluate with a real end-to-end timing breakdown (load/etl/embed stage durations) before committing to the added complexity.
notes: Added per-stage timing breakdown (sqlite_read/embed/chroma_upsert) to generate_and_store_embeddings, logged at end of each run. Issue stays OPEN until a real indexing run's breakdown is captured and reviewed to decide if overlap is worth the complexity.
close_reason: Measured with real instrumentation added for this issue (per-stage timing in generate_and_store_embeddings). Two full 4269-product reindex runs post-DirectML-fix: ETL ~2m38-39s, embed-loop ~26-27.5s total with sqlite_read=0.0s (0%), embed=23-24.5s (89%), chroma_upsert=2.9-3.0s (11%). SQLite read time is negligible/unmeasurable, so there is no meaningful I/O to overlap with compute — embed-loop is compute-bound on ONNX/DirectML inference, not I/O-bound. Producer/consumer prefetch would add complexity for no measurable gain. Not pursuing.

title: Verify DirectML actually executes inference (not just selected) via ORT profiling
description: After fixing the onnxruntime-directml install-order bug (daz-content-browser-0ce), Windows GPU performance counters showed zero usage for vab.exe during a live indexing run, raising doubt about whether DmlExecutionProvider was genuinely executing compute or just reported as 'active' by session.get_providers() (which only reflects configured/available providers, not actual per-node execution). Added an opt-in diagnostic (EMBEDDING_PROFILE_PROVIDERS=1) using ONNX Runtime's own execution profiler to log per-provider node count and duration. Verified inside the actual frozen vab.exe (not just the dev venv): DmlExecutionProvider executes 1616 of 2212 graph nodes, CPUExecutionProvider only the remaining 596 (normal unsupported ops like reshapes). Same split confirmed in both the venv and the bundled executable. Conclusion: DirectML is genuinely active; the earlier zero-GPU-counter reading was a Windows performance-counter sampling artifact (misses brief/bursty workloads), not a real CPU fallback.
acceptance_criteria: EMBEDDING_PROFILE_PROVIDERS=1 diagnostic added to embedding_utils.py, off by default; verified via test_embedding.py and tests/test_api.py passing; provider split confirmed identical in dev venv and frozen vab.exe.
close_reason: Confirmed via ORT execution profiler inside the actual frozen vab.exe: DmlExecutionProvider runs 1616/2212 graph nodes, identical split to the dev venv. GPU question settled - DirectML is genuinely active.

title: Quantize ONNX model to reduce DIM package size

Applying ONNX dynamic quantization to int8 would reduce it to approximately 300-400MB, bringing the total DIM zip from ~900MB to around 400-500MB. Use onnxruntime.quantization.quantize_dynamic with QuantType.QInt8. Should be added as a step in export_model.py with a --quantize flag, and evaluated for search quality impact.
